#1615. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Livramento drives the ball 60 yards looking for Barnes but the ball skids off the turf and into Trafford’s arms.

Crunching Bard tackle on Bamba sends the ball to James who lets fly from 22 yards into the shins of a Newcastle defender.

Bard is penalised for a trip on Barnes as the game peters out.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

Wissa escapes a booking for a snide kick at Muharemovic’s shin.

A debatable offside call which should have been left for VAR lets Trafford off the hook when he comes out of his area to clear a ball clipped over the top. He slices it to Toure and the ref stops the game but I think Bard was playing Wissa, who found Toure, onside.

Newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Willock hooks a half-volley on to the roof of the net.

Bard → GudmundssonAaronson → OkaforWilson → Tanaka

Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

There was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

Gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle quickly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

You could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not currently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

From the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Leeds United Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Stach, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin. Substitutes Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, James, Bahoya, Nmecha.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; González, L Miley; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa. Substitutes Pope, Livramento, Schär, Bamba, Steur, Touré, Willock, Ramsey, M Miley.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

#1614. Fonseca revisits bitter Milan exit: “I didn’t even get a phone call”

Paulo Fonseca has strongly hinted at being unhappy with how his experience at AC Milan came to such a sudden end.

Fonseca joined Milan ahead of the 2024-25 season, tasked with replacing Stefano Pioli who had won a Scudetto and reached a Champions League semi-final. However, he did not even last until the end of the year before being sacked after a draw with Roma.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It wasn’t a very well-kept secret that the Portuguese was under pressure, and it didn’t take long until Sergio Conceicao replaced him in what seemed to be a manoeuvre orchestrated mainly by agent Jorge Mendes.

Fast-forwarding to the past week, Fonseca abruptly left Lyon in order to return to Portugal with Sporting CP, with whom he signed a contract until 30 June 2030. He takes the place of Rui Borges, and during the press conference (via Calciomercato.com) he revealed some details.

“I think there was a phone call. It happened around the time the rumours started circulating that Rui had refused to speak to me.

“Yesterday I had the pleasure of speaking with him: it was a very open and honest conversation, between two coaches who perfectly understand, without any hypocrisy, what moments like these mean.

“We spoke at length, very pleasantly, with great mutual respect and admiration, as I’ve said before. I didn’t just speak with Rui, but also with his assistant, Tiago, whom I’ve known for a long time. Sometimes controversy arises when, in reality, things are completely normal.

“I can tell you this story. I was at Milan, we were playing against Roma, and the coach who would replace me had already been hired [Conceiçao]. The next day I had to quickly clear out my room and locker because the new coach wanted to come in.

“And you know what? I didn’t even get a phone call, but there was no need. In football, these situations are part of the game, and I didn’t take it personally. We must understand, without hypocrisy, that these processes are natural.”

#1613. Newcastle Confidential: REVEALED - Players 'confused' by Matthias Jaissle's instructions, why formation tweak is a possibility, Joelinton injury worry and new transfer guru's methods explained

Published: 12:00 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 12:01 EDT, 4 November 2026

Newcastle’s players are ‘confused’ by what Matthias Jaissle wants from them, a source close to the dressing room has told me.

I've been told the squad remains supportive of Jaissle and there is a determination to get things right for the head coach – senior players accept there is a responsibility on them – but there is also a desire for clarity over what it is they are being asked to do on the field.

Jaissle said in the wake of Monday's 1-0 home defeat by Everton that he could not understand why the team had not followed his instructions and executed the tactics they had worked on in training. He said the plan was not to play ‘long balls’.

Sources also say Jaissle spoke to his players afterwards about their press not being what he wanted and their passing being too slow in the opposition half.

However, I have been told some players are unsure as to the playing style and strategy, and that has led to those in deep positions getting the ball forward as quickly as possible, invariably with a long pass. There are also some within the dressing room wondering why the team continues to play with a No 10 when they do not have a specialist in that position.

Another source close to a senior player says the logical solution is a return to the 4-3-3 of recent seasons. There was word from inside the training ground that Jaissle was considering such a change ahead of the trip to Crystal Palace last month, so it is not off the table.

The demand from supporters to find a place for teenager Sean Steur in the midfield could yet see a tweak to the system, especially as Jaissle believes he and Nico Gonzalez are not suited to playing together as a two.

Newcastle's players are understood to be 'confused' by what it is head coach Matthias Jaissle wants from them

The demand from supporters to find a place for teenager Sean Steur (left) in the midfield could yet see a tweak to the Newcastle system

Joelinton is a fresh injury concern and medical staff will know in the next 24 hours if he is set to miss Saturday’s trip to Fulham, I can reveal. The Brazilian was feeling some muscle discomfort post-match on Monday and there is hope that the issue is related to a severe case of cramp.

However, I understand that is yet to be confirmed and, given Joelinton’s history of muscle strains, including his hamstring, no chances will be taken. The 30-year-old only returned from a thigh injury three weeks ago having been sidelined since the summer.

In better news, Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Lewis Miley are set to return for the game at Craven Cottage.

I understand Fernandez-Pardo wanted to be included in the squad for the visit of Everton but was told by staff he needed more training. The Belgian had missed the previous two matches with what is being described as a ‘tricky virus’ and only returned to training over the weekend.

Fernandez-Pardo arrived on Tyneside insisting he wanted to be used as a central striker following his £51million move from Lille. However, Jaissle currently prefers William Osula in that position and Fernandez-Pardo will likely be competing for a place out wide at Craven Cottage.

Miley, meanwhile, was also pushing for involvement on Monday after recovering from a glute issue. The 20-year-old’s return is timely given the midfield struggles of late, as well as the fresh worry over Joelinton and Jacob Ramsey’s suspension following his red card against Everton.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is available again for Newcastle after suffering with a ‘tricky virus’

One player who almost certainly won’t come in for a start is Aladji Bamba, although we are told he will NOT be going out on loan in January.

The 20-year-old has appeared for just 27 minutes since his £30m arrival from Monaco in the summer, and he has not featured at all since September 19.

But despite potential availability issues in midfield, Jaissle does not feel Bamba is ready to start Premier League matches. That has led to a suggestion among some that he could be loaned out in January, especially as he has made only 12 senior starts in his career.

However, I understand the plan is for Bamba to remain on Tyneside and there has been encouragement with his recent performances in training.

Aladji Bamba has impressed in training of late and won't leave on loan in January despite his lack of first-team minutes

It has been interesting speaking to those who know a little more about Newcastle's new head of recruitment Tomas Amaral, who was virtually unknown in the UK before his appointment last month.

The Portuguese, 35, has been described as a 'bookworm and laptop obsessive', a meticulous talent-spotter who works long into the night. Amaral, who spent four years scouting for Benfica and was most recently sporting director at Spartak Moscow, has also spoken previously of the dangers of clubs signing good players who do not fit the manager's system.

He believes recruitment should begin with a clear footballing identity, rather than collecting talented individuals and hoping they somehow fit together. He also argues that scouts should challenge managers over transfer targets, rather than simply indulge their wishes.

Interestingly, his recruitment strategy involves two lists – one identifying players good enough for the club, the other those specifically suited to the manager's demands. For him, character and adaptability are considered just as important as ability.

He was part of the Benfica scouting team who identified Enzo Fernandez when signing him from River Plate in 2022. The midfielder was sold to Chelsea for a near £100m profit the following year.

Amaral’s arrival at least gives clarity to the recruitment structure inside St James’ Park, and he would appear to have a busy 12 months ahead given what feel like obvious areas for improvement across the pitch. I understand there is scope to spend in January should the club feel it necessary.

Beneath first-team level, Newcastle have cast their scouting net a little wider this week with two promising teenagers from Gambia arriving on Tyneside.

We understand Omar Marong and Alieu Saine, both 16, will stay for a two-week trial and train with the academy. They are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and have been identified under the club’s new global talent drive.

The pair caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while winger Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals. Neither player can join permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle are keen to assess their potential.

Meanwhile, the club are also set to appoint a specialist scout in Africa.

Finally, Newcastle prospect Matheos Ferreira could soon be at the centre of an international tug of war.

The 18-year-old, born in Ashington and raised in Berwick, has been called up by Brazil Under 20s for friendlies against Japan and Singapore this month. He is the only English-based player in the squad.

Newcastle prospect Matheos Ferreira could play for England, Italy or Brazil

But Ferreira, whose father is Brazilian and mother Italian, also qualifies for England and Italy. He has previously represented England at youth level and recently obtained an Italian passport.

I have seen him play a handful of times and there is certainly plenty of talent and potential. Interestingly, he has been operating as a No 10 at times this season, having come through the ranks as a winger.

Maybe there is a No 10 inside the club after all…

#1612. Sunderland vs Chelsea - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 06 Nov 2026 14:33, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 17:48

Needing nothing short of a minor miracle to replicate their 2025-26 feats against Chelsea, Sunderland host the Blues in Sunday's Premier League fixture at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats trail their visitors by 16 places and 11 points in the Premier League table at the time of writing and face Xabi Alonso's well-rested men after a sobering defeat in Europe too.

The meeting between two erstwhile Premier League midfield maestros last weekend saw Alonso pile more misery onto Michael Carrick, whose Manchester United side had the better of the opening 45 minutes at Stamford Bridge before an all-too familiar implosion.

Morgan Rogers waltzed his way past a disorganised Red Devils defence to propel the Blues into the lead, before Lisandro Martinez's senseless red card and Cole Palmer's penalty put paid to any hopes of a Mancunian fightback.

Snapping a two-game losing sequence in all competitions and earning their third win from their last four Premier League matches, Chelsea's triumph coupled with Liverpool losing to Arsenal saw the Blues consolidate fourth spot in the rankings, one clear of the Reds and three worse off than Brighton & Hove Albion.

The Blues' sorry defeat to Tottenham Hotspur raised questions about how Alonso's squad can cope in the absence of influential attacker Joao Pedro, but Chelsea answered those critics in gameweek nine to earn their first Premier League home win with a clean sheet since January.

Fifteen goals conceded still makes the visitors the worst defensive unit in the top 10, though, while they have shipped eight in five away games in all tournaments; seven of those came in their first three road matches, though, and they have since allowed just one in their last two on rival turf.

However, Alonso's side now square up to one of the four teams with a worse backline tally than them in the 2026-27 Premier League, and one without Chelsea's colossal firepower to make up for it.

The second season syndrome cliche is very much appropriate for Sunderland, whose measly five-point total places them bottom of the Premier League standings, although 17th-placed Man United are only two points better off.

The Black Cats have shown little signs of survival spirit in recent weeks, though, as last weekend's humbling 3-1 loss to newly-promoted Coventry City marked their fifth defeat from their last six Premier League games and extended their winless run in the division to seven.

Stadium of Light was also awash with boos on Thursday night, when Regis Le Bris's men went down 2-0 to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League, ending their unbeaten start in the tournament and leading to renewed sack talk.

The Sunderland hierarchy are not minded to remove Le Bris from his post just yet, though, and the Frenchman's focus now turns to repeating last season's shock 2-1 home and away wins against Chelsea, but not since 2001 have the Black Cats bested the Blues in three straight games.

Chelsea boss Alonso confirmed a triple fitness boost in his pre-game press conference, revealing that Emiliano Martinez is in contention to return from his jaw operation, while Aaron Anselmino and Jordan Henderson have battled back from injury and illness respectively.

The latter's presence may be crucial this weekend, as Moises Caicedo missed training earlier this week due to discomfort, and there are no guarantees that he will be fit to face the Black Cats.

Jorrel Hato (unknown), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) Reece James (knee), Jamie Gittens (ankle) and Joao Pedro (quad) are confirmed absentees for Chelsea, whose playmaking star Cole Palmer will have a particular point to prove this weekend after being omitted from Thomas Tuchel's England squad yet again.

As for a jaded Sunderland side, Omar Alderete serves a one-game ban following his sending-off at Coventry, but Nordi Mukiele should exit concussion protocols in time to deputise for his fellow defender.

Daniel Ballard (hamstring), Habib Diarra (muscle) and Romaine Mundle (knee) will not return before the international break, though, while teenage striker Juan Riquelme Angulo is uncertain due to a contact injury.

Le Bris ripped up his second-string side in midweek, making no fewer than four half-time changes, so expect the likes of Trai Hume, Reinildo, Enzo Le Fee, Noah Sadiki and Brian Brobbey to return here.

Roefs; Hume, Mukiele, O'Nien, Reinildo; Xhaka, Sadiki; Rigg, Le Fee, Angulo; Brobbey

Penders; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Palestra; Henderson, Lavia; Estevao, Palmer, Rogers; Neto

Fatigue should not play a significant role for Sunderland on Sunday given the alterations Le Bris made in midweek, but backing the Black Cats to get anything out of any Premier League game at present is a tough ask.

Therefore, even a Pedro-less Chelsea side - working on a full week's worth of rest - should stroll to victory, with an increasingly familiar clean sheet in tow.

A Jurgen Klopp favourite could be about to save Liverpool.

It's a new era for the Reds. The Andoni Iraola era has started relatively positively, but one cannot deny the last two games against Arsenal and Fenerbahce have somewhat tainted the overall outlook on the Spaniard.

Liverpool may have spent lavishly in the last few transfer windows, but the reality is that expectations should be tempered when it comes to Iraola.

He has inherited a squad that lacks overall balance, and it will take time for him to fix the gaps. Liverpool will likely need to invest more in the upcoming transfer windows, too.

But what Iraola has done with what he has at his disposal is admirable. Liverpool are playing exciting football again. The Reds are scoring goals and the passion has very clearly returned to the side.

Andoni Iraola discovers his biggest challenge at LiverpoolNaturally, Iraola will have known that he wasn't coming into a perfect situation. Liverpool visibly struggled under Arne Slot last season. The environment around Anfield has been toxic, to say the least. But now that Iraola has managed to turn the attitudes and the atmosphere around, there is one clear challenge that he simply needs to get right. Undoubtedly one of the biggest obstacles for Iraola if he wants to be successful is to get the best out of Florian Wirtz. Liverpool have essentially built the team around the German and so far Wirtz has struggled to adjust to the pace and intensity of the Premier League. He does have time to turn things around but at the same time Liverpool won't exercise patience forever.

#1610. Brest vs Lyon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 06 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:33

On a mission to record back-to-back wins, Brest welcome title-chasing Lyon to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Sunday afternoon for a Ligue 1 contest.

Les Pirates picked up a comfortable success at Lorient last time out, whereas Les Gones have been busy on continental duty, sharing the spoils at Real Sociedad.

After a mediocre 12th-placed finish in Ligue 1 last season, Brest are aiming to qualify for European competition this time around, with their recent form suggesting that a continental charge could be successful.

Les Pirates have lost just one of their past four top-flight matches after picking up a 2-0 away triumph at Lorient on Monday night, when Ludovic Ajorque and Noah Edjouma found the net in the second half.

Aiming to record consecutive top-flight victories for the first time since early March, Brest are currently occupying 10th position in the Ligue 1 standings, eight points behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain.

Rather surprisingly, only four of Les Pirates' 12 league points have been collected at Stade Francis-Le Ble so far this campaign, with Julien Lachuer's men winning only one of their opening four home contests.

That sole success was impressive and emphatic in equal measure, though, as leading marksman Ajorque provided a goal and an assist in a 5-1 battering of relegation-threatened Angers on October 10.

Following back-to-back wins over Anderlecht and Conference League champions Crystal Palace to commence their Europa League campaign, Lyon have earned just one point from clashes with Hoffenheim (0-3) and Real Sociedad (1-1).

In fact, Les Gones have won just one of their past four matches (D1 L2) across all competitions, with their most recent away league outing ending in a 2-0 victory for PSG at Parc des Princes.

However, Jorge Maciel's troops were able to strengthen their faint title hopes last Sunday afternoon, when goals either side of the half-time break from Ernest Nuamah and Corentin Tolisso were enough to beat Angers.

That success extended their unbeaten home league run to five matches (W4 D1) and moved Lyon up to third position in the Ligue 1 table, just three points behind Luis Enrique's European champions.

Les Gones are unbeaten across their past three encounters (W2 D1) with Brest; however, Les Pirates are unbeaten in the past three meetings (W2 D1) between the sides at Stade Francis-Le Ble.

Brest are expected to be without the services of Brendan Chardonnet, who is sidelined for up to two weeks because of a calf problem.

Les Pirates' options at centre-back are further reduced by the absence of 20-year-old Raphael Le Guen.

A high-profile loanee from Juventus, Lois Openda is currently in the Lyon treatment room because of a leg injury.

With the Belgian set to return after the international break, Nuamah is an important source of goals this weekend for Les Gones.

Wanted by Championship side Wrexham in the summer, Pavel Sulc is out until January with a knee injury.

#1608. Opinion: Julian Ward has found Liverpool someone even better than Milos Kerkez

Liverpool's left-back situation has quickly become a major problem for them.

Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have both failed to meet expectations with fans now getting rather used to both players being subbed off for one another in the middle of games.

When Tsimikas plays, fans miss Kerkez and when Kerkez plays, fans miss Tsimikas. It ends up being an endless cycle of Liverpool trying to figure out who their best left-back actually is.

Obviously, Kerkez was one of Andoni Iraola's best players at Bournemouth during the 2024-25 season with the Hungarian even being crowned as the Premier League's best left-back that season.

Since then, that version of the 22-year-old has failed to show up, which, when Liverpool spent around £45 million on signing him, is far from ideal.

His poor form has led to many questions being asked by fans with Julian Ward now having to go out of his way to find potential replacement options for the former Bournemouth man.

Archie Brown is now on Liverpool's radar as a potential left-back option

As mentioned, Liverpool are suffering with their left-backs at the moment.

Some fans are actually still questioning why Andy Robertson was even allowed to leave for nothing at the end of last season.

Because, even though he may have been getting on a bit, he still played a regular role in Arne Slot's team and, from the vast majority of his performances for Tottenham this season, he'd have been a better option than what they have right now.

Indeed, Tsimikas is expected to leave on a free at the end of this season so, change is coming but, right now, it's unclear who could be targeted.

Many different players have been linked but, thanks to an update from TEAMtalk, Fenerbahce's Archie Brown looks like an option that Liverpool want to explore.

"Archie Brown scored and provided an assist to help Fenerbahce beat Liverpool in a famous 3-2 victory in Istanbul – against a side who have been monitoring the left-back and now look poised to ramp up their interest, TEAMtalk can exclusively reveal," they wrote.

"His contribution will have been particularly interesting for Liverpool, who TEAMtalk understands have been carrying out work on the defender this season as they assess potential options at left-back.

"However, the Merseyside club are far from alone in their admiration of the former Gent man.

"TEAMtalk understands that Brown has attracted interest from several Premier League sides, with Chelsea having had him on their radar last year through the BlueCo recruitment network.

"Manchester United have also been monitoring his progress regularly, while Newcastle United, Everton and Brighton are among the other clubs understood to have kept tabs on his development."

Archie Brown is a better left-back than Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez

Brown may have been born in Birmingham but, he's spent almost all of his professional football career outside of England.

The left-back has played for numerous clubs across the world with his current club, Fenerbahce, the highest profile of the lot.

Throughout his career, he's been used all the way down the left-hand side of the pitch but, thanks to his defensive capabilities and his speed, he's sort of settled into his role as a left-back.

Thanks to his time with Derby as a youngster, he'd be classed as homegrown which, for Liverpool, is a massive bonus.

Much like Kerkez, Brown is only 22 so he has a lot of his career ahead of him but, even just after his performance against the Reds in the Champions League on Wednesday, it's clear that he'd be a better option for Liverpool to have at their disposal.

And, with Tsimikas' contract set to expire soon, he'd be a perfect option for Liverpool to explore.

#1606. Revealed: How Arsenal have used NASA to tackle their injury woes - with Google and Apple joining the fight

Published: 12:00 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EDT, 4 November 2026

Mikel Arteta has often stretched the boundaries of quirkiness in his pursuit of excellence at Arsenal - and it can now be revealed that his search for those marginal gains has seen the club quite literally reaching for the stars.

Injuries are once again the focus for Arteta after Bukayo Saka sustained a thigh strain at Bayern Munich two weeks ago. He is expected to be ruled out for four to six weeks. It is the 25-year-old’s 11th injury since September 2024.

Arsenal have been blighted by injury, and Arteta has been fixated on reducing the problem ever since the 2022-23 campaign - where William Saliba’s absence cost them dear in the Premier League run-in.

But what are they doing to fix it? Daily Mail Sport can reveal that Arsenal staff have in recent seasons been tasked with reaching out to blue-chip companies, seeking innovative ways which could help lower the number of injuries and accelerate recovery.

Earlier in Arteta's Arsenal reign, NASA were consulted on their expertise in space physiology, specifically in relation to ACL injuries.

In space, the reduced load on the human body – because of less gravity – contributes to muscle atrophy and bone density loss. As a result, NASA have conducted extensive research into what happens to the body under reduced gravity, and how it responds when back on Earth.

Injuries are the one area that Mikel Arteta has been unable to solve in his quest to find marginal gains

Bukayo Saka went off inside 10 minutes at Bayern Munich last month, having suffered his 11th injury in just over two years

Arsenal believed there could be valuable lessons to apply to their ACL rehabilitation process. This includes exploring areas such as how much weight an injured player should bear at different stages, how quickly that load should be increased, how reduced-gravity exercise can allow players to resume running and loading movements earlier, and how to measure whether a player’s body is actually tolerating those increased demands.

The issue has been particularly pertinent given Arsenal's experiences in recent seasons. Jurrien Timber ruptured his ACL on his Premier League debut against Nottingham Forest in August 2023, ruling him out for nearly nine months, and Gabriel Jesus spent 332 days out when he suffered the same injury in January 2025.

The problem has not been confined to the men’s team. Arsenal women's side have also endured a troubling run of ACL injuries, with several high-profile players affected in recent seasons. Leah Williamson, Beth Mead, Vivianne Miedema and Victoria Pelova all suffered ACL injuries in the 2022-23 season, while Manuela Zinsberger, Michelle Agyemang and Katie Reid have all had the same injury in the past 18 months.

NASA aren’t the only high-tech addition to Arsenal’s crackdown on injuries. It’s understood that Google, one of the club’s official partners, were consulted on data analytics. The company’s expertise in processing vast quantities of information could help identify patterns associated with injury risk, spotting subtle changes in running mechanics or physical output.

Similarly, Apple were consulted about using wearable technology to collect physiological data and build a clearer picture of how players respond to training and rehabilitation. This included the use of Apple Watches to track metrics such as heart rate and exercise intensity.

Arsenal’s global brand helps in these partnerships. It’s ultimately a passport into world-leading organisations, who are often intrigued by the prospect of working with a major sports side.

How effective Arsenal's attempts have been is difficult to measure, as a multitude of factors contribute toinjuries, some of which are out of the club’s control. The number of players injured at Arsenal in recent years, though, have suggested a disproportionate problem compared to other sides.

One noteworthy example, given what has happened since, is the Champions League match against Club Bruges on December 10, 2025. Seven players were out: William Saliba, Gabriel, Cristhian Mosquera, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz, Leandro Trossard and Max Dowman. It took Arsenal’s injury total at that stage to 95 (excluding Rice’s illness) since the start of the 2024–25 Premier League season – only Brighton had more (97).

Jurrien Timber was struck down with an ACL injury in his Premier League debut in August 2023

Gabriel Jesus also suffered an ACL injury in January 2025, ruling him out for almost the entire calendar year

William Saliba's injury in March 2023 proved fatal for Arsenal's title charge, with Rob Holding unable to play in the same high line as Manchester City hunted the Gunners down

The club instigated a mass medical team shake-up last summer kickstarted by the appointment of Spanish physio Joaquin Acedo, a long-term Arteta associate from when he was a Real Sociedad player over two decades ago. Among the other new arrivals are head of medical services Dr Arnaldo Abrantes and physiotherapist Carmen Marquez, who both joined from Aston Villa, head of player rehabilitation Eneko Angulo and fitness coach Jose Jimenez.

A slogan on the wall in Arsenal's medical room which reads: ‘Your best ability is availability’ says it all.

This season, Arsenal have not yet been as badly affected by injuries. Aside from Saliba and Saka, Christos Tzolis, Ben White and Mosquera have all spent time out, while Eberechi Eze recently picked up an unspecified injury.

It is the impact of missing key players at crucial times which has irked Arteta the most. While the 2023 title charge was killed off when Saliba had to be replaced by Rob Holding, who was unable to maintain the same high line and press, the 2024-2025 season fell apart when Jesus and Havertz were injured in January, leaving only midfielder Mikel Merino to play up front.

Last term Havertz started just seven league games after damaging his knee ligaments in the opener at Manchester United.

Perhaps the most Arteta-like thing about all this is that, even after turning to NASA, Google and Apple for answers, the search for an edge never really stops.

#1605. Opinion: Liverpool positioning massive agreement, ends Richard Hughes disaster plan

Liverpool are reportedly considering a move that would bring an end to a Richard Hughes disaster deal. They're getting into position.

Liverpool made some massive deals in the Richard Hughes era. How many have actually worked out? That's entirely up for debate but most would land on "not many".

Some of those deals were record-breaking signings, of course. Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola are all nine-figure arrivals and we're yet to see the best from any of them. Even if Isak is finally scoring goals quite regularly.

It wasn't just the signings, though. Hughes also struck big-money contracts and that included deals for Mohamed Salah and Virgil van Dijk within the first year of his appointment as sporting director.

Hughes didn't even wait another year before deciding he wants out of the Salah deal. The Egyptian left early with a year remaining on his contract. Did that put him off more big contracts, though?

One of the final major decisions that Hughes made was licking in Liverpool's future midfield. Or at least, locking in the foundation of it.

That meant renewing both Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai for enormous contracts. It also meant not renewing Alexis Mac Allister even though the Argentine actively sought a new deal.

The decision was made. Liverpool committed to the former pair as the stars of their midfield and Mac Allister would move on, possibly even last summer. That latter part didn't happen and now it seems that the club are ready to go back on Hughes's plan.

The Athletic reports that Liverpool are actually coming around to the idea of renewing Mac Allister after all. It would be a rejection of that initial plan, with the club willing to admit that he's a core part of the short-term future in midfield.

It also questions the futures of Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, just months after their deals. If Mac Allister is to be renewed as a starting midfielder, after all, what are they? They received guarantees under the previous sporting director, after all, in order to sign the contracts.

But it seems Liverpool may have had a change of heart. They're positioning themselves, even if it's only slightly, for a Mac Allister deal. It would be a massive decision - and one that makes a very harsh comment on the end of the Hughes era.

#1602. Report: Andoni Iraola is about to miss out on Liverpool's next Virgil van Dijk

Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool's head coach has been a bit mixed.

While the Spaniard may have only lost three games across all competitions this season, it still feels like the Reds could have done a lot better than they have.

They should have put up a much tougher fight against Manchester City and Arsenal than they did but, because they didn't, they're now fifth in the Premier League table.

Wednesday's 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce proved how far the Reds still have to go before they're treated as genuine challengers for silverware again.

So, in order to push them towards achieving this goal, the January transfer window may have to be a busy one with the Reds already being linked with many different moves.

Chelsea want to offer long-term Liverpool target Levi Colwill a new contract

Liverpool's defence may have had a lot of work done to it in the summer but, there are still several changes that need to be made before its back to its best.

Virgil van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo have all performed to a fairly high standard but, with Van Dijk's contract set to expire in June 2028, change is clearly afoot.

Indeed, the Reds could end up offering the Dutchman a new deal but, right now, that doesn't feel all that likely.

This has led to several different players being linked with a Liverpool move with some causing genuine excitement to emerge from fans.

However, as per a fresh update from TEAMtalk, one of the Reds' long-term targets, Levi Colwill, looks likely to be offered an extension to his current terms with Chelsea.

"Chelsea are ready to open discussions with Levi Colwill over a new contract, with an extension for their homegrown defensive star expected to become a priority in 2027 amid interest from Liverpool, TEAMtalk understands," they wrote.

"The Blues are keen to secure the long-term future of the 23-year-old, who has established himself as one of the Premier League’s most impressive young defenders since breaking into the first team in 2023.

"Brighton were particularly keen to secure Colwill on a permanent basis following his successful loan spell at the Amex Stadium, but Chelsea made it clear they had no intention of selling.

"Tottenham and Liverpool have also made approaches for the England international, only to encounter a similar stance from the Blues.

Levi Colwill would have been perfect for Liverpool

Not only do Liverpool need extra depth among their ranks right now but, they also need to add a fair few homegrown players to their ranks.

Thanks to how many foreign players the Reds have in their squad, they physically can't register anymore players other than homegrown ones.

This is obviously a massive problem with Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa both missing out on all of their Champions League games as they're not registered to play.

Colwill is one of many centre-backs who would have been a solid acquisition for Liverpool.

However, there's just something about the Englishman that makes him feel like a perfect successor for Van Dijk.

He's tall, fast and strong. Three of the key things about Van Dijk's game.

And, since he's only 23 years old and has already featured in 86 Premier League games, there's plenty of room for him to grow while already having a decent chunk of experience under his belt.

Here's hoping that the Blues don't actually offer the versatile defender a new deal so that the Reds can finally get their man.

#1601. Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer speaks out to reveal his 'enormous pain' and says he will 'face whatever comes' after police opened homicide investigation and fans called him 'murderer'

Published: 11:22 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 13:47 EDT, 4 November 2026

Jesus Owono, the goalkeeper involved in the fatal collision with the late Jesus de Miguel, has spoken for the first time since the tragic incident.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono collided with opposing striker de Miguel in the latter stages of a hotly contested 2-2 draw with Tenerife in Spain's second division on Monday.

De Miguel immediately collapsed following the devastating blow in which Owono's knee appeared to strike the forward in the chest. He passed away in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

Owono has since shut down his Instagram account amid the significant backlash he has received – which saw him subjected to chants of 'murderer' by the Tenerife fans as he left the pitch – but he has now issued a statement alongside his club.

'FC Andorra continues to be deeply affected by the death of Jesús de Miguel,' they wrote. 'In these very difficult moments, our player Jesús Owono wishes to personally share a few words.'

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

Jesus Owono has broken his silence after being involved in a fatal collision with Jesus de Miguel

Tenerife striker de Miguel died on Tuesday morning following the horrifying clash with Owono

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús.'

The club added: 'FC Andorra asks for the utmost sensitivity and respect.'

Andorra held a minute's silence at the club's training ground today, and the collision has opened the debate surrounding challenges involving goalkeepers and outfield players in football.

Former Real Madrid and Spain international goalkeeper Santiago Canizares, speaking on El Partidazo de COPE, conceded he believed Owono used ‘excessive force’ when going for the challenge.

Canizares, however, offered a defence of Owono by explaining the goalkeeper’s likely thought process and explained that they typically use their knees as protection and to help avoid collisions.

‘It's a goal-scoring opportunity, and what Owono has in his head is “I have to contest that ball,” ball or player,' Canizares said.

‘For me, the problem is that Owono uses excessive force, and he lacks the physical dexterity to pull himself back when he sees he's won the duel.

‘He goes all out and goes all out until the end. That physical dexterity is key when only one of the two is contesting.

‘What happens in this case is that I think the momentum causes the knee to rise due to the force and excessive speed it brings.’

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

FC Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz has also defended his team-mate, writing that the goalkeeper has been 'deeply affected' by the tragedy.

'There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be,' Spatz wrote in a statement shared on social media.

'What we went through is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless, and with a sadness that is difficult to explain.

'First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’s family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family. Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch.'

Spatz continued: 'I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is. We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

'In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.'

Police investigating de Miguel's death are now probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged yesterday homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Police are investigating the death of de Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

But overnight it emerged the police probe will also review the medical response to Monday's emergency and seek to address questions about whether de Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch and whether a defibrillator was used from the outset as well as issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

The 30-year-old father-of-one died on Tuesday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

#1599. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”
