#1525. Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Sloppy Reds wilt in Turkey again as Dirk Kuyt masterminds famous Champions League win against his error-strewn old side

Published: 14:54 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:15 EDT, 5 November 2026

The mad metropolis of Istanbul was the setting for one of Liverpool’s greatest nights, when this storied old club won the 2005 Champions League final down the road at the Ataturk Stadium – but right now fans will be glad to see the back of Turkey for a while.

For the third time in just over 13 months, the English giants have travelled to the bustling hub on the banks of the Bosphorus only to wilt amid the deafening noise of a Turkish football stadium.

They lost twice to Galatasaray last season and now, over the river to the Asian side of the intercontinental Istanbul, Liverpool fell flat at the hands of Fenerbahce – thanks to two Englishmen and a friend-turned-foe in the dugout.

Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown, born in Bradford and Birmingham respectively, both scored for Fenerbahce before Vedat Muriqi scored a winner as caretaker manager Dirk Kuyt, once a cult hero at Anfield, recorded a win in his final game in the dugout.

He will soon be replaced by ex-Newcastle and 101-cap Turkey midfielder Emre Belozoglu but Kuyt will not be forgetting this evening in a hurry in front of a raucous, hostile crowd in the district of Kadikoy.

As for Liverpool, who jetted home straight after the game and were due to land around 2am English time, they and boss Andoni Iraola were just glad to get out of Turkey, probably with their ears still ringing.

It was a poor night for Liverpool as they went down 3-2 against Fenerbahce in Istanbul

Andoni Iraola's side let a second-half lead slip and there were some terrible errors

Archie Brown sunk to his knees in celebration at full-time as the home crowd erupted

Trey Nyoni had scored his first goal in professional football and then Alexander Isak headed home to put Liverpool 2-1 up two minutes after coming on as a substitute but they were undone by sloppy defensive errors.

That will give Iraola plenty to ponder in the coming weeks given his side have conceded nine goals in their last three European games, all to opposition that would not be counted as part of the continent’s best in LASK, Villarreal and now Fenerbahce.

Aside from a UEFA Super Cup triumph over Chelsea at the home of Besiktas in 2019, Liverpool have struggled in this country and their last Turkish delight came against Trabzonspor, who now employ a certain Mohamed Salah, back in 2010.

Fenerbahce and Kuyt celebrated a famous win – as did around 45,000 home fans who produced deafening whistles every time Liverpool had the ball.

It was a true attack on the senses and Iraola’s side felt it, with several passes going astray as Kuyt’s men had the best of the first-half action and were unlucky to go into the break level at 1-1.

Liverpool had gone ahead on 25 minutes through Nyoni’s first goal in professional football, when a header from English full back Brown fell straight into the path of the Reds midfielder, who charged on to the ball like he was Steven Gerrard.

He needed a deflection off defender Kojo Peprah Oppong but cared not a jot as his volley ended up beating former Manchester City man Ederson.

It continued a stellar season for 19-year-old Nyoni, who has had a fairytale week that included a first Premier League start, first professional goal and also talks over a bumper new contract. To say it would be deserved would be the understatement of the season.

Trey Nyoni opened the scoring for the Reds but his goal came in a losing effort

Alexander Isak headed Liverpool back in front after some terrible Fenerbahce defending

FENERBAHCE (4-3-3): Ederson 5; Semedo 5 (Muldur 75), Skriniar 6, Peprah 6, BROWN 8; Guendouzi 7, Kante 7, Yuksek 5; Greenwood 8 (Aydin 89), Lukaku 7 (Muriqi 63, 6), Kahveci 7 (Arturkoglu 75).

Subs not used: Cetin, Gunok, Efe Demir, Mercan, Elmaz, Nene, Mimovic.

Scorers: Greenwood 29, Brown 73, Muriqi 79.

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 4; Gomez 5 (Wirtz 66, 6), Jacquet 5, Van Dijk 4, Tsimikas 4 (Kerkez 76); Nyoni 8 (Koumas 85), Mac Allister 7; Munoz 5 (Isak 66, 6), Szoboszlai 5, Ngumoha 7 (Gakpo 67, 6); Barcola 5.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Araujo, Chambers, McConnell, Danns.

Nyoni’s goal, in theory, should have helped Liverpool settle. As it was, it did anything but.

Fenerbahce came out roaring and hit the bar instantly through Irfan Can Kahveci. With the next attack, they were level, just four minutes after falling behind.

Just like Liverpool’s goal, the Turkish side needed a hefty deflection to help them. Greenwood took a free-kick from 25 yards, Jeremy Jacquet turned his back on it and foxed Alisson. Two Brazilian goalkeepers, two wicked deflections that neither could do anything about.

Alisson was the best away player on the pitch in that opening 45 minutes, thwarting Greenwood, the brute force of Romelu Lukaku and fellow former Premier League favourite N'Golo Kante, who is now 35 but still has the energy of the young whippersnapper we all knew and loved.

Iraola turned to his bench with a £285million triple-change and two of them combined just minutes later, Cody Gakpo crossing for Isak to head home his seventh of the season.

But just as when they went 1-0 ahead, Liverpool retreated and invited pressure. A Kante cross was not dealt with by Gakpo and Brown could ghost in at the back post to score.

Then, on 79 minutes, Muriqi thumped home a header to put Fenerbahce 3-2 up and on their way to a memorable night.

Liverpool, who would have taken a huge step towards qualification with a win here, still have work to do.

#1524. Barcelona's 'new De Bruyne' impresses alongside Lamine Yamal

By Naim Beneddra | 06 Nov 2026 17:39

Barcelona have found an unexpected solution to their defensive injury crisis in a young midfielder once compared to Kevin De Bruyne, whose remarkable relationship with Lamine Yamal is now proving valuable to Hansi Flick.

Brian Fariñas, 20, has impressed in his first two senior appearances for the Catalan giants, operating at right-back despite spending most of his development at La Masia in midfield.

The academy graduate made his competitive debut in Barcelona's 6-1 victory over Alaves on October 31 before retaining his place for Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League success against Aston Villa.

His performances have already earned praise from Flick, but a new account from his former youth coach has revealed an intriguing story behind his development.

Fariñas was once nicknamed 'Fabruyne' because of his technical qualities, while his close friendship with Yamal stretches back to their earliest years together in Barcelona's academy.

Fariñas joined Barcelona's youth system in 2018, arriving as a relatively shy youngster before gradually establishing himself as one of La Masia's most promising midfielders.

His development took an important turn when he began playing alongside Yamal in the club's youth teams.

Iván Carrasco, the coach who first brought the pair together, has revealed that the two became virtually inseparable.

"They were like two peas in a pod. They used to get up to all sorts of mischief at La Masia," Carrasco told Mundo Deportivo.

"They went everywhere together. They were always playing jokes in the dressing room. They developed a really good connection and have got on brilliantly ever since."

Their friendship continued even as their careers progressed at different speeds.

Yamal made his first-team breakthrough at 15 and quickly established himself among Barcelona's most important players, while Fariñas continued developing in the academy.

The latter regularly attended matches at Camp Nou in the seats reserved for players' relatives and friends, and even travelled to Germany to watch Yamal help Spain win Euro 2024.

Carrasco also revealed that Fariñas possessed attacking qualities that earned him an unusual nickname during his youth career.

"I used to call him 'Fabruyne'," the former Barcelona coach explained, referring to Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne.

The comparison came from Fariñas's ability to use both feet, move inside from wide areas and strike powerfully from distance.

"He can use both feet, which is very interesting when you're playing on your natural side. He can cut inside and shoot with his left," Carrasco added.

"He has a stepover that you'll see plenty of. It's like the one De Bruyne used to do."

The former coach believes Barcelona supporters have yet to see the full range of Fariñas's attacking abilities, particularly his shooting from outside the penalty area.

Originally developed as an attacking midfielder, the youngster also featured on the wing before gradually moving into deeper midfield positions.

He was an important member of Barcelona's Under-19 side that completed a domestic and European treble in 2024-25, before establishing himself with Barça Atlètic under Juliano Belletti.

Last season, he contributed five goals and six assists in 35 appearances for the reserve team.

Those performances helped convince Flick that Fariñas deserved a place in his senior plans, with the German reportedly intervening during the summer to prevent a proposed move to Girona.

Fariñas's route into Barcelona's starting lineup has been particularly surprising because the opportunity arrived in a position he had rarely occupied.

Injuries to Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart left Flick with limited defensive options ahead of the Alaves match.

Rather than selecting a more experienced player out of position, the Barcelona manager handed Fariñas his senior debut at right-back.

Fariñas completed 100 of his 103 passes against Alaves, recorded 114 touches and demonstrated impressive composure despite facing unfamiliar defensive responsibilities.

His ability to move forward and combine with Yamal also caught Flick's attention.

"He connects very well with Lamine. That's very important," the German explained after the victory.

"He helped us a lot in that position. He deserved these minutes because he's very professional and always focused in training."

Fariñas himself acknowledged the significance of the support he received from his teammates, particularly Yamal.

"They gave me confidence," he said after his debut, referring to the assistance provided by the players around him.

Four days later, Flick retained the youngster against Aston Villa, giving him a first Champions League appearance against Premier League opposition.

Fariñas again looked comfortable in possession, completing 11 passes in the attacking third, a figure matching Pedri's contribution in that area.

His understanding with Yamal helped Barcelona maintain attacking combinations down the right without sacrificing the defensive discipline required of a full-back.

The partnership represents an unusual reunion for two players who once operated together much further forward in La Masia.

While Yamal has become one of the world's most exciting wingers, his childhood friend is now providing support from behind him.

With Kounde still recovering from an ankle problem, Fariñas could receive another opportunity when Barcelona visit Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

Flick has not suggested that the youngster will permanently replace the French international, but his emergence gives the German another option in a defence repeatedly disrupted by injuries.

For a player once known for his resemblance to De Bruyne, the chance to establish himself at the highest level may have arrived in a position few expected.

#1522. Woltemade involved in both goals but VAR denies Lucumí as Juventus draw 2-2 with Rennes

Nick Woltemade created Juventus's opener and scored their equaliser, but Jhon Lucumí's late winner against Rennes was ruled out for offside. The draw in Turin moves Spalletti's side to seven points in the Europa League league phase ahead of Sunday's trip to Lecce.

Juventus came within a VAR decision of beating Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday 22 October. Jhon Lucumí found the net in the 90th minute. Referee Morten Krogh studied the pitchside monitor and disallowed the goal for offside. Eight minutes of stoppage time followed, and the match finished 2-2.

Nick Woltemade was central to both Juventus goals. Spalletti’s side now sit on seven points after three league-phase matches. They had lost 0-3 to Lazio in their previous game.

Zeki Çelik put Juventus ahead in the fifth minute from Woltemade’s pass. Mousa Al-Tamari equalised in the 15th minute, set up by Bryan Reynolds. Federico Gatti was booked in the 19th minute for stopping the Rennes goalkeeper from taking a quick clearance.

Weston McKennie hit the post at around the half-hour mark with the score still level. Rennes then won a penalty when Douglas Luiz was penalised for handball. Boulaye Dia converted it in the 43rd minute, and the visitors led 1-2 at the break. Çelik, the scorer of the opener, went off injured after 45 minutes. Al-Tamari earned the match’s top rating from the data provider, 8.2.

The equaliser came from the spot. Reynolds blocked a Nico González header with his arm away from his body, and VAR upheld the award. Woltemade scored the penalty in the 67th minute. He finished with seven shots and two key passes.

Juventus generated expected goals of 2.25 against 1.72 for Rennes. They also had 54% of possession. Rennes took more shots, 16 to 14, and put more on target, five to four. Juventus were caught offside three times, while the visitors were never flagged. Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal was booked in the 82nd minute for time wasting.

Both sides were short of key players. Spalletti was without the injured Locatelli, Yildiz, Thuram, Grabara, Ekhator and Conceição. Zhegrova and Milik were unavailable because they are not on the UEFA squad list. Antonio Stefano Merola was in the 21-man squad after his first senior call-up. Rennes were missing their leading scorer Lepaul, who was injured and did not travel from France.

FT |⌛️| Finisce in parità all’Allianz Stadium#JuveSRFC #UEL pic.twitter.com/QaF2LuUDp9

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 22, 2026

Krogh had refereed nine Europa League matches and one Champions League match before this game. He had never taken charge of either club.

Juventus’s next Europa League fixtures are away to AZ Alkmaar on 5 November 2026 and at home to Omonia on 26 November 2026. Before that, Serie A resumes. Lecce host Juventus on matchday 8, with Eusebio Di Francesco’s side kicking off against Spalletti’s at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday 25 October.

#1521. Brighton & Hove Albion vs Brentford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 18:08, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 22:32

High-flying Brighton & Hove Albion will welcome Brentford to the Amex Stadium for Sunday's Premier League encounter.

The Seagulls head into the weekend in third spot in the Premier League table, while the Bees start matchday 10 in sixth position.

Brighton are a surprise team in the Premier League title picture after winning six, drawing one and losing two of their nine top-flight matches this term.

Fabian Hurzeler's side demonstrated they are capable of bettering the Premier League's biggest teams in last Saturday's away meeting with Manchester City, which saw Yasin Ayari score the decisive goal in a 1-0 victory as Brighton got revenge for their EFL Cup loss to the Citizens just a few days earlier.

The victory moved them to within two points of second-placed Man City and kept them within five points of leaders Arsenal.

Brighton's domestic success has been made all the more impressive by the fact they are balancing it with a Conference League campaign, in which their latest outing yielded a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Getafe in Thursday's trip to Spain.

After moving up to fifth spot in the league phase, the Seagulls will now return to the familiar surroundings of the Amex Stadium, where they are yet to lose this season after winning five and drawing one of their six home matches in all competitions.

All five of those wins have produced clean sheets and at least three goals, including a statement 5-0 victory in their most recent home outing against rivals Crystal Palace.

Brighton head into Sunday's fixture with an unbeaten Premier League home record against Brentford, having won three and drawn two of their five top-flight meetings at the Amex Stadium.

Brentford, meanwhile, are sitting two points adrift of the top four after winning three, drawing five and losing just one of their nine Premier League games this season.

While the Bees are firmly in the hunt for European football, they returned from the international break with a four-game winless run in all competitions before they got back on track in last Saturday's home clash with Nottingham Forest.

A Nikola Milenkovic own goal sent Keith Andrews's side into the break with a slender advantage, before Igor Thiago scored in a second straight game to wrap up all three points at the Gtech Community Stadium.

The Bees will head on their travels with hopes of recording back-to-back Premier League victories for the first time since beating Aston Villa and Newcastle United at the start of February.

That will be easier said than done for a team that has gone nine consecutive away league games without a win, although they have at least proven to be tough to beat after drawing each of their four Premier League road trips this term.

If they are to claim a long-awaited win, they will have to beat Brighton at the Amex Stadium for the first time since picking up a 2-0 victory in the Championship in September 2016.

The visitors will at least fancy their chances of striking first, having netted the opener in eight of their nine Premier League matches.

Brighton & Hove Albion Premier League form:

Brighton & Hove Albion form (all competitions):

Brighton remain without the services of Kaoru Mitoma, Stefanos Tzimas, Zadok Yohanna and Evan Ferguson.

Pascal Struijk and Femi Azeez are making progress in their respective injury recoveries, but Sunday's contest is likely to come too soon for the pair.

Full-back Ferdi Kadioglu, who has missed the last three games with a hip issue, is understood to have a chance of proving his fitness in time for the home fixture.

If he is ready to feature, the Turkey international will likely replace Costinha in what could be the only change made to the side that started last Saturday's win over Man City.

As for the visitors, Andrews has reported no fresh injury concerns, although he is unable to call upon a number of players, including Rico Henry, Kaye Furo, Josh Dasilva and Fabio Carvalho.

Antoni Milambo has been training regularly as he closes in on a return from a long-term injury absence, but he is not expected to be risked at the Amex Stadium.

The Brentford boss will welcome back Yehor Yarmoliuk, who is in contention for a starting spot after serving a three-match ban.

Jaidon Anthony is also pushing for a starting berth after coming off the bench to provide an assist for Thiago's goal in the win over Nottingham Forest.

Brighton have scored at least three goals in each of their five competitive home wins this season, and while Brentford have drawn all four of their away league games this term, we think the Seagulls will make full use of their firepower to extend their unbeaten head-to-head home run with a relatively comfortable victory.

Lenny Joseph scored twice in the second half which gave Ferencvaros a memorable night at San Siro, but it was one that their performance merited in truth. The Rossoneri threw big names on in the second half but were unable to break the visitors down, even after they got a red card.

“We lacked attitude right from the start. We needed to react immediately and not wait to take hits. They created opportunities through our mistakes.

#1519. Man United news: Lisandro Martinez should not play for the Red Devils again

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 18:27, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 18:31

Ahead of Manchester United's Premier League clash with Aston Villa on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses the 20-time English champions.

The Red Devils are without a win in the Premier League since the end of August but managed to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

If they go and get beaten here, it undoes all the good work from the Roma match. It was just an extraordinary game. Those two goals going in, the Soule goal and then the Malen penalty, and you just thought here we go again.

As Mick McCarthy said, it can get worse. At half time, that was probably as bad as I have felt as a Man United fan for a while. There have been some bad moments over the last 14 or 15 years, but you just thought they were never going to win a game again.

Then you have a turning moment, and it was the Fernandes penalty: he missed it, then the retake, and it goes in. It just takes little moments in football.

Roma have previous in the Champions League this season of not being able to hold on to a lead. It was happening against Real Madrid as well. They must have smelt blood. They must have felt Roma had mistakes in them. It was not Roma's first-choice goalkeeper between the sticks either. They did not test him in the first half at all.

But then the penalty goes in, and you think: what are they made of? Cunha was one that took the game by the scruff of the neck, quite literally late on.

He took his shirt off for the yellow card and then got sent off with a bad tackle late on, but you do not mind that. The fans certainly do not mind seeing that aggression, which has been lacking all season.

Shea Lacey has to come in down the right for this game. Amad Diallo is a good footballer, nice and tidy, but he has not scored a goal in going on a year now, and that is just not good enough. He missed a big one at Chelsea last weekend.

Shea Lacey has to come in down the right. He played that lovely pass to Cunha for the 3-2 goal late on. He was bright, he wanted the ball, and he has to come into the team.

Patrick Dorgu is back in training, and it will be very interesting to see whether he is fit enough to start. If he is, I would like to see a reshuffle at the back: Dorgu at left back, Dalot over to the right, with Yoro and Maguire in the middle.

Martinez is suspended, and Heaven is struggling at the moment. I do not want to go too overboard on Heaven. He has had a lot of criticism, but he is only 20 years old and is just not ready, probably not good enough, to be a starting centre back at Man United at this moment in time, and that is fine. He can supplement the squad.

Carlos Baleba will be facing a lengthy period out. Tielemans as a straight swap, or Santos as an option alongside Kobbie Mainoo. Mbeumo, Cunha and Fernandes: I expect them to start again.

I do not think there will be too many changes, but I would like to see those ones because they just need more down the right, where the fullbacks have struggled this season.

The defeat to Chelsea: Man United played really well in the first half but just could not get that goal. They did get a goal through Cunha that was rightly disallowed for offside, but it was so disappointing at that moment.

The Martinez incident: I said a few weeks ago after his comments about the Champions League game that I did not want him to play for the club again, and I do not want him to play for the club again now. That was unforgivable. He has lost his head. He is going to leave the club, whether that is this summer or the next.

Whether you release him or look to sell him, I do not want Martinez playing for Man United anymore. He has let the club down badly and there is no coming back from that.

Try to get a centre back in January, and next summer Man United need to sign three or four defenders. Can Marcus Rashford get himself fit for this game? Probably unlikely. Luke Shaw is still out. Sesko is still out.

But there is a chance now for them to go and beat Aston Villa, a good Aston Villa side, on Sunday afternoon, and then go into the international break in a positive mood.

I read a report recently that apparently Didier Deschamps has been contacted as a potential name, one that has not been at the forefront of many people's thoughts at this stage.

I still expect Carrick to leave at some point, whether that is after this game, in two months' time, or at the end of the season.

I do not expect Michael Carrick to be the manager of Manchester United for the next five years.

The reports at the moment suggest there would not be an interim, so it is unlikely he will go and then someone be brought in next summer.

It looks like they might try to keep Carrick in the job for as long as possible until they identify that next appointment. I wrote a piece recently about Cesc Fabregas and Man United.

After that Como win in the Champions League, I would like to see Fabregas as a long-term option at Manchester United. Deschamps would be a very interesting candidate as well.

Carrick got his stay of execution last time out. He needed that result, and inside he would have been absolutely buzzing with what he saw in that second half.

Man United cannot go two down in this game. If they go two-nil down, they are in big trouble. They need to score first on Sunday.

Go and get a win, go into the international break with more positivity ahead of the Liverpool game at Anfield straight after. Big games to come: Sporting Lisbon away in the Champions League at the end of the month.

I expect Carrick to stay at the moment. If they get beaten here and it is a bad one, he could go. Really interesting times, but a good win last time out and finally a little bit of positivity.

#1518. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

Sources: Juventus FC, Tuttosport, Virgilio Sport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1517. Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Our 125 anniversary & one of the best days! 💫 pic.twitter.com/YbZLTFPpWN

I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season.

Pascal Gross pulling the strings. 🔎 @Microsoft pic.twitter.com/DAgVsG2B3W

Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions in three consecutive seasons.

Like Everton, Newcastle labour to a home win which should have been more comfortable. It would have been had Wissa scored his penalty, but it was a nervy finish as Hull pushed for an equaliser after Cho’s goal.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

One of the outstanding team performances of the season so far from Brighton, and it will take some beating between now and May. Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

Kai Havertz shoots straight at the goalkeeper when clean through, and that is surely Arsenal’s last chance of an unlikely comeback gone. Brighton have pushed Arsenal back for much of the season half, they have not been sitting on a lead.

At St James’ Park, Hull have pulled a goal back through Cho to set up a nervy finish for Newcastle.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

What a farcical five minutes we have had, from an absurd disallowed goal for Everton to a ridiculous red card for Abdul Fatawu, banished for a second bookable offence - which was diving. There is going to be plenty said about Thierno Barry’s second goal being chalked out because, when you see it, you will wonder what it was for. These are the situations with which I struggle most - if players do not appeal for a wrongdoing, if they don’t feel they have been the victims of an injustice, why are officials getting involved?

Thierno Barry thought he had made it two for Everton, but the goal has been ruled out because Brennan Johnson was judged to be interfering with play and offside. You’re never getting those this weekend after the Enzo Fernandez incident.

Arsenal undone from a corner, swung to the back post and Chema Andres rose above everyone to head home.

This is a remarkable performance by Brighton, who have battered and bullied the champions from the start. Three-nil, and they have even beaten Arsenal at their own game by scoring a set-piece.

I am struggling to remember the last time Arsenal were overrun and outplayed as comprehensively as this. It’s a thrashing.

No half-time subs from Mikel Arteta, which is a little surprising given Arsenal’s predicament.

The undisputed highlight of the afternoon so far – Raspberry Beret has just been played during the half-time interval and you will agree that this is Prince’s finest work. The memories of that defeat are clearly still fresh in the minds of the Brighton supporters, who are roaring with rage at every perceived delay by the visitors, despite the fact that Arsenal are losing. The bad blood is adding to the intensity of the occasion.

Ipswich don’t play like a team that is short of confidence and quality. You might assume, if you haven’t seen much of them, that they are destined for a season of toil but there is definite quality with Gary O’Neill’s ranks, including Abdul Fatawu, who has been magnetic in drawing your eye to him. They might be a goal down but they are playing as if they are a goal in front.

Arsenal had just enjoyed a spell of control, but trail to a goal from one of the league’s in-form players. Gross whips a shot from just outside the box around Raya and in off the post.

Brighton have the lead at the Amex and it’s their captain, Pascal Gross, who has provided it. Superb long-range effort, in off the near post. On the overall balance of play, Brighton deserve that. It’s reward for their courage and willingness to go after Arsenal, rather than sitting back.

It took almost 20 minutes but Arsenal have found their feet in this game now. They are starting to find avenues through Brighton’s aggressive pressing and have made a few promising runs in behind, through Havertz and Saka. This is a high quality match.

No goals at the Amex, but Brighton are the team making the running, Arsenal struggling to play out from their own half and are yet to register a shot on goal.

Barry kept himself onside and turned the ball into the back of the net with his stomach. He did well to avoid a handball.

Bright start from Everton and they have the goal they deserve, albeit it came in fortuitous circumstances. James Tarkowski’s volley clattered into Thierno Barry and the deflection took it away from Christian Walton in Ipswich’s goal. Barry now has five goals for the season and, while he is raw, it’s an invaluable contribution.

A storming response to a bad night at Leeds from Newcastle, and it looks like being a long afternoon for Hull. Two down in seven minutes.

What a start for Newcastle United and what will really please manager Matthias Jaissle is the way both goals have come from his players winning important tackles.

The German was incensed by the lack of physicality and intensity in the heavy defeat to Leeds on Monday but the first goal for Joe Wilock came when Lewis Miley won a tackle on the edge of the Hull penalty box.

The second came when Sven Botman came away with the ball just inside his own half. On both occasions Harvey Barnes provided the assist. A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The home team are pressing high and all over Arsenal in the early stages. Raya has just made a save to deny Kostoulas.

Brighton have started brilliantly against the champions. They are hunting like wolves, pressing Arsenal with remarkable intensity. We have played seven minutes and I don’t think the ball has left Arsenal’s half.

Big chance for Everton to take the lead, but after great skill to turn his man at the edge of the box Brennan Johnson shoots wide with only the goalkeeper to beat.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

We are under way at the Amex, St James’ Park and the Hill Dickinson.

Another famous face in the stands at Hill Dickinson Stadium today but this time it’s not about politicians. Wayne Rooney is here to watch his boyhood club and he will be hoping Everton can go into the international break unbeaten. An extra special cheer too before kick-off for Jarrad Branthwaite, who has just been called up for England duty. Plenty of Premier League clubs would like to sign Branthwaite, if they were given half a chance, but David Moyes has made it quite clear that Branthwaite: “Isn’t for sale - I want to keep my best players.”

He was not part of the match-day squad at Sunderland but Ben White’s injury has opened up a place, and Dowman fully deserves it after his two goals against Ipswich in the League Cup. Sam Dean has the story of his rise to stardom as well as what Arsenal are doing to nurture such a special talent.

Brighton are wearing a special “125 anniversary” kit today, to mark 125 years since the club was formed in 1901. It’s inspired by the colours of their first ever kit, which means an all-blue shirt, pale gold shorts and dark socks. Personally I would not allow such nonsense. But I don’t make the rules.

Spurs scored two late goals to salvage some pride against Aston Villa, but it is another defeat for Roberto De Zerbi’s team who have two points from five games. This Emi Buendia screamer put the game out of reach.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the new buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; L Miley, Botman, Thiaw, Hall; Steur, Willock; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Pope, Schar, Bamba, Toure, Thompson, Pivas, Salia, M Miley, Mills

Hull City XI: Tzolakis, Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Herrington, Giles, Belloumi, Crooks, Slater, Thomas, McBurnie

Subs: Phillips, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, McNair, Stroud, Gourna, Iroegbunam, Vaz, Cho

We are getting to the stage where we really need to start asking questions about Tino Livramento’s injury record.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring issues.

Injuries are already cutting deep into the Newcastle squad, with four teenagers on the bench for the visit of Hull. None have played in the first team before and three of them – Michael Mills, Mason Miley and Kyrian Thompson are just 17–years-old.

Newcastle wanted a younger team this season but not this young. It was interesting to hear Matthias Jaissle talk before the game. He knows how tough this season could be with so little experience in the side.

Subs: Scherpen, Furlong, Greaves, Florentino, Nunez, Akpom, Flemming, Philogene, Maeda

Lewis Dunk is a surprise absentee for Brighton, it can only be because of injury, and Hurzeler has preferred Diego Gomez to the lively Yalcouye who was very threatening at Old Trafford and Coventry. He could be a handful off the bench.

Good news for Arsenal: Jurrien Timber is finally fit enough to start a match again. This is his first start since mid-March and his return is timely, given the absence of Ben White through injury. It’s also a first Premier League start for Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes, who comes into the midfield after his impressive performance off the bench at Sunderland last weekend.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Bruno G, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis

Subs: Steele, Hadjam, Rutter, Promise, Osman, Costinha, Svoboda, O’Riley, Yalcouye

The one he wore in Only Fools and Horses episode Yuppy Love. Of course, Bloom could actually talk about his wealth rather than one of those old five pound notes he found the other day...

Very excited for this one today. Arsenal have won all seven of their matches so far. Only once before in their history have they won their first eight games of a season - that was in 1903, when they were playing in the Second Division as Woolwich Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/iNBxoHl4Gc

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

#1516. Caykur Rizespor vs BB Erzurumspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:55

Caykur Rizespor will be looking to end their five-match winless run when they welcome BB Erzurumspor to Caykur Didi Stadium on Sunday, with the visitors hoping to return to winning ways after suffering a home defeat in their previous Super Lig outing.

The hosts sit 13th in the table with 11 points from 10 matches, three points behind the 11th-placed visitors, who have collected 14 points.

Rizespor's recent results have left Recep Ucar with plenty to address, as his side were held to a goalless draw by Kocaelispor last time out, although that point came after three consecutive defeats against Trabzonspor, Corum and Fenerbahce.

Their winless run began with a draw against Goztepe, marking a significant decline from their opening five league matches, during which they recorded three victories.

Their struggles at home are an even more pressing concern, with Rizespor losing all four of their matches at Caykur Didi Stadium this season, conceding 10 goals and scoring just three, leaving them as the only team in the league yet to collect a point on home soil.

They will make another attempt to change that record in what will be their first top-flight meeting with Erzurumspor since 2021, with both sides having recorded one victory each in their four previous Super Lig encounters, alongside two draws.

Erzurumspor won the most recent meeting between the teams, securing a 2-0 victory in the Turkish Cup earlier this year, and are unbeaten in their last two encounters with the hosts (W1, D1).

However, the Serkan Ozbalta's men arrive after suffering a 3-1 home defeat to Corum, which ended a four-match unbeaten run across all competitions (W3, D1).

They will be eager to bounce back immediately on the road, having recorded a positive result in their most recent away fixture, a 3-1 victory over Gaziantep that also marked their first away win of the campaign.

Erzurumspor have also won just once in four previous visits to this ground, losing twice and drawing once, suggesting that Sunday's encounter could prove difficult despite Rizespor's poor home form.

Rizespor are expected to be without Khusniddin Alikulov, who is recovering from a knee injury, while Can Bozdogan is also unavailable with an ankle problem.

Modibo Sagnan is suspended, leaving Ucar with defensive adjustments to make, while Ahmed Kutucu has also been listed as a potential absentee, although his availability remains uncertain.

Erzurumspor are likely to be without Mustafa Yumlu, who is struggling with a muscle injury, although the visitors otherwise appear to have fewer significant availability concerns.

The visitors have scored nine goals in their opening 10 league matches, with Eren Tozlu and Miguel Cardoso contributing three apiece, and both forwards will be hoping to add to their tallies as they prepare to lead the attack.

Caykur Rizespor possible starting lineup:

Gorgen; Pala, Mocsi, Bakayoko, Ariss; Diakite; Mebude, Olawoyin, Laci, Bulut; Gennaro Borrelli

Taskiran; Ovacikli, Gerxhaliu, Kirtay, Mujakic, Giorbelidze; Baiye, Owusu, Rodriguez; Cardoso, Tozlu

With neither side particularly convincing defensively, a closely contested draw looks a reasonable outcome, especially given Rizespor's difficulty turning home advantage into victories.

Erzurumspor have shown enough quality on their travels to trouble the hosts, but their own recent setback suggests they may have to settle for a point.

#1514. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Sources: Juventus FC, Juventus FC broadcast guide, Flashscore

#1513. Çorum Belediyespor vs Fenerbahce - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:56

Fenerbahce will be looking to build on an important European victory when they travel to face Corum Belediyespor at Corum Stadyumu in the Turkish Super Lig on Sunday.

Former captain Emre Belozoglu returned to the club as head coach earlier this week, taking charge of a side sitting sixth in the table with 16 points from 10 matches, level on points with their hosts, who occupy seventh place.

Corum have made a respectable start to life in the Super Lig, winning half of their 10 league matches this season to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

After failing to win any of their opening three fixtures, the Red-Black have gone on to collect five victories in their last seven matches, with their most recent success coming in a 3-1 win away to Erzurumspor.

That victory followed their defeat to Goztepe, continuing a recent pattern in which they have responded to each of their last two league defeats with a win in their subsequent fixture.

Burak Yilmaz's side will nevertheless be aware that their defensive organisation faces a much sterner examination on Sunday, having conceded 16 goals in their opening 10 league matches, the most of any team in the top eight, although only four sides have scored more than their 21 goals.

They have scored just six of those goals at home and conceded four, while drawing two and losing two of their four matches at Corum Stadyumu this season.

Sunday's encounter will be the first meeting between the two sides, and Corum will hope to make a positive start to this new fixture, although doing so will require them to record consecutive home victories for the first time this season.

Fenerbahce, meanwhile, arrive with renewed confidence after recovering from a difficult spell to beat Liverpool 3-2 in the Champions League, with Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and Vedat Muriqi all finding the net.

That result followed consecutive 2-1 defeats against Goztepe and Galatasaray in the Super Lig, a difficult run that preceded Ismail Kartal's departure and Belozoglu's decision to leave Kasimpasa for a second spell in charge of the Yellow Canaries.

The new coach inherits a side that has produced some impressive attacking performances, with only Amed SK (25) scoring more goals than Fenerbahce (24) in the Super Lig, although their inability to turn that attacking quality into consistent victories has left them with five wins from 10 league matches and nine points behind leaders Galatasaray.

Another concern heading into Sunday's clash is their recent away form, having lost their last two competitive matches on the road and conceded in both, with their most recent setback coming against Galatasaray in the league.

Çorum Belediyespor Turkish Super Lig form:

Corum will be without Gokhan Sazdagi, who is suspended after picking up a booking in the victory over Erzurumspor.

Emircan Gurluk is also sidelined with a muscle injury, while Fredy remains a doubt after struggling with a similar problem.

Jesus Ramirez has been one of Corum's most reliable attacking players, scoring six league goals this season, and is expected to lead the line alongside Ermin Mahmic.

Fenerbahce also have several selection concerns, with Nathan Ake and Marco Asensio carrying injuries, while Jayden Oosterwolde is expected to miss out with an Achilles problem.

Archie Brown is suspended following his involvement in the post-match physical brawl against Fenerbahce, while Kojo Peprah Oppong remains a doubt.

One of Belozoglu's biggest decisions will be who leads the attack, with Romelu Lukaku competing with Muriqi, who has scored seven league goals this season and also found the net in the Champions League victory.

Çorum Belediyespor possible starting lineup:

Felipe; Sazdagi, Soyuncu, Smolcic, Borza; Under, Ramadani, Diomande, Kyziridis; Mahmic, Ramirez

Ederson; Semedo, Skriniar, Peprah, Mercan; Kante, Guendouzi; Kahveci, Yuksek, Greenwood; Lukaku

Corum have enough attacking quality to make this an uncomfortable afternoon for Fenerbahce, but the visitors should have sufficient depth and quality to find a way through.

Their confidence will also be boosted by the important European victory in midweek, and we expect Belozoglu to make a winning start to his second spell in charge.

#1512. Viktor Gyokeres shows he still has an important part to play for Arsenal after starring role in win over Slavia Prague as Mikel Arteta begins next phase of his masterplan, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 17:03 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:19 EDT, 5 November 2026

The next phase of Mikel Arteta’s season masterplan was seemingly underway: get the Arsenal frontline firing.

The plaudits for a defence which has conceded just eight goals across the Premier League and Champions League are well endorsed.

Yet, as Viktor Gyokeres was making a compelling case for challenging Kai Havertz’s spot, Arteta’s backline decided to have a temporary, rare malfunction.

By full-time Slavia Prague’s winless streak in the Champions League had reached 23 games — the joint-worst ever in the competition alongside AEK Athens, despite a late onslaught which momentarily caused the visitors jitters. Slavia boosted their shot count up to 17, compared to Arsenal’s 12. The north London club had taken their eye off the ball having reached half-time two goals up.

David Raya was called upon for a world-class save, using his full frame to dive and deflect Oskar Kubiak’s header onto a post.

Wiktor Nowak then pulled a goal back on 90 minutes from inside the area having collected substitute David Jurasek’s pass to tap home near the goalline.

Noni Madueke celebrates scoring the opener for Arsenal against Slavia Prague

Viktor Gyokeres netted the second for the Gunners with this curling effort

Nowak had another chance, as he went agonisingly close to a further Jurasek cross. Such laxness by Arsenal would be punished elsewhere in Europe, though they still remain unbeaten in the Champions League after four matches.

An annoyed Arteta said: ‘It was two very different halves. The first one, where we played at a really high level. It should have been three, four or five (goals).

‘Right from the beginning (of the second half), we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we had to do, in every concept.

‘I already mentioned a few things and some others that I will keep to myself.’

Even without William Saliba, who made the squad for the first time this season following a back injury sustained at the World Cup in July, the Gunners have usually been imperious in defence.

It’s their attack which has its fair share of holes, not helped by Bukayo Saka’s thigh injury and the lack of an in-form No9.

Yet, a bit of love and persistence can do wonders for a striker — and could be the antidote Arteta needs to rejuvenate Gyokeres, who caused Slavia a migraine with both his footwork and finishing.

Behind the Bane mask Gyokeres figuratively wears in his celebrations lies a man whose confidence has taken more than a knock or two.

Mikel Arteta made six changes to the Arsenal side that beat Liverpool at the weekend

Having struck 21 goals across all competitions last season, the Swede has largely occupied the bench in the current campaign.

Yet, the two pieces of play Gyokeres executed on a chilly Prague evening showcased just why he has an important part to play this season for Arsenal.

David Raya’s aerial punt accidently found its way to Gyokeres, following a defensive mishap, which the striker chested down.

SLAVIA PRAGUE (4-2-3-1): Domchak 5; Vlcek 6, Holes 6, Zima 6, Kubiak 5; Moses 6, Sadilek 6; Ayaosi 5, Sulieman 5, Sturm 5; Nowak 7.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 7; White 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Hincapie 6; Zubimendi 6, Rice 7; Madueke 7, Merino 7, Eze 7; Gyokeres 8.

Instead of recycling the ball — an easier option for a man still finding his way — he went for the maverick option, producing a well-executed flick-on which found Noni Madueke. The winger reached the area, fending a defender off, before coolly slotting home.

Then before the break, Gyokeres had a goal of his own. After a neat one-two with Declan Rice, the Swede stormed into the box, before curling the ball in off the post from inside the area.

For all his deficiencies and limited chances thus far, the moment felt important for a striker who has now struck two goals and three assists in his past five appearances.

Havertz is Arteta’s No1, but one striker won’t be enough to properly sustain a campaign by which the league title and a first Champions League trophy in the club’s history are viable aims.

Even Madueke, enjoying a prolonged run on the right wing in Saka’s absence, was in inspired form.

Arteta made six changes to the Arsenal side that beat Liverpool at the weekend, with Merino earning a start on the ground where he exactly one year ago struck a second-half brace in Arsenal’s 3-0 victory against Slavia Prague last November.

Daniel Toula scored late on for Slavia Prague but they were unable to find an equaliser

Merino had his shot tipped over the bar after Madueke’s opener, the pressure already being felt by the home side.

Eberechi Eze went on a jinking run, featuring a nutmeg to the delight of the visiting fans, and it was all getting rather open.

The Gunners were close to going three goals up, Gabriel’s effort cleared off the line after Nazar Domchak spilled the ball.

Slavia suddenly came to life in the final minutes and had Arteta fretting on the touchline. An extraordinary turnaround was in sight.

Nevertheless, the form of Gyokeres will be a positive Arteta can take from a night not at his usual standards.

#1511. Douglas Luiz finally opens his Juventus account as Spalletti hails display at Lecce

Douglas Luiz has finally scored for Juventus. The Brazilian midfielder found the net in Sunday’s 2-0 win at Lecce, more than two years after his €50m move from Aston Villa, and he also set up the opening goal for Weston McKennie.

It was a night that changed the conversation around a player who has spent much of his time in Turin under scrutiny. Luciano Spalletti was quick to single him out afterwards, and the club’s own numbers show just how rare an evening like this has been for him.

According to the standout stats published by Juventus on Monday, this was the first time Douglas Luiz had both scored and assisted in the same match in Europe’s top five leagues. Before Sunday he had made 261 appearances in those competitions without managing it.

The club also points out that he now has two goal involvements from eight Serie A appearances this season, one goal and one assist. In the 2024/25 campaign he played 19 league games for Juventus and failed to register either.

Both contributions came before the break. His free kick was dinked over the Lecce defence for McKennie to break the offside line and slide in on 29 minutes. Twelve minutes later, Federico Gatti laid the ball off and Douglas Luiz hit it first time from outside the box into the far corner.

Douglas Luiz’s first goal in Bianconero! ⚪⚫ pic.twitter.com/g2vTIhUEnF

JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 25, 2026

The midfielder did not dwell on the personal milestone. In comments shared by the club’s press room after the game, he put the result first.

“The most important thing today was to win. I’m really happy with the result because we’ve worked so hard, and I’m delighted for the team. This victory also gives us the confidence we need,” he said.

He was also honest about the second half, when Lecce pushed Juventus back. “We played well in the first half, but I think we could definitely have done better in the second. We need to improve and perform well for the full 90 minutes.”

Speaking to DAZN, he added that the set piece routine involving Teun Koopmeiners is something the squad practises a lot, and that the players were pleased for their coach after a difficult week, as Tuttosport reported.

Spalletti had already explained after the 3-0 defeat by Lazio that he wanted changes, as covered in our piece on the changes Spalletti identified. Since then Juventus have moved to a three-man midfield, and Douglas Luiz has been one of the beneficiaries.

Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the coach was full of praise for the Brazilian. “He had a great game today, he fought and ran, he battled on all sides and he helped clean up certain situations when we needed him to,” Spalletti said, in quotes reported by Football Italia.

He came off after 82 minutes, replaced by Sarr, having done the bulk of the work in a side that had only 17 outfield players available. With Manuel Locatelli and Khéphren Thuram among the absentees listed in our latest injury update, Spalletti needs exactly this kind of reliability from his remaining midfielders.

One good night does not settle a debate that has followed Douglas Luiz since his arrival. What it does give him is a platform. If he can keep producing this level of energy and quality in a system that suits him, the midfielder who struggled to make an impact in his first season may yet become an important figure for Spalletti this term.

Sources: Juventus FC, Football Italia, Tuttosport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1510. GdS: A ‘true disaster’ – scrutiny intensifies as Milan sink to new low in Ferencvaros loss

AC Milan fell to a third Europa League defeat in four games last night at San Siro, losing against Ferencvaros who maintained their perfect start.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report by asking the obvious question: what is the real Milan? Is it the aggressive, focused and at times dazzling side seen in the derby at the weekend, or the listless, disjointed, and sterile team witnessed yesterday against Ferencváros?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In all likelihood, the real Milan are both – doomed, partly due to structural limitations, to oscillate between positive performances and lacklustre displays. To be clear, the Rossoneri won’t get far in any competition this way, as there can be no ambition without consistency.

Their last six matches have been a constant see-saw between victory and defeat. On only one of five occasions have Milan managed to come back from a deficit, a sign of a profound struggle to react.

Yesterday, their Europa League campaign became dangerously complicated: direct qualification for the next stage is now little more than a pipe dream, and even reaching the play-offs is hanging in the balance.

As things stand, Milan would be eliminated, and the schedule includes a daunting away trip to face Olympiacos and a home match against Sunderland, followed by two theoretically easier fixtures. The ‘Version A’ of Milan would have no trouble finishing in the top 24, but ‘Version B’ risks falling short.

One must also ask how much they truly care about the Europa League. While it is true that the squad lacks depth and injuries provide a valid excuse, Amorim’s team selections made it clear that Sunday’s away match in Genoa was considered the higher priority.

Yet, making such choices hinders growth. So far in Europe, the Diavolo have delivered three embarrassing performances in four games in Europe. It is a hard pill to swallow, but this is Milan: an international competition cannot be treated like a midweek friendly.

The match against a very good Ferencváros side was handled poorly: a terrible approach, an overly convoluted tactical set-up (even accounting for absences, which must be considered but do not justify such absolute mediocrity), and a complete lack of intensity.

It was as if the players were still suffering from a hangover following their derby celebrations. Amorim opted for a 4-2-3-1 formation, tasking Jashari with orchestrating play, while relying on the pace of Hutchinson and Cissé to disrupt the disciplined Hungarian defence.

The problem, however, was that there was no bow from which to launch those arrows. Jashari once again displayed a concerning lack of personality. Borbely assigned Bero to mark him, and that move alone was enough to reduce the Swiss player to performing only the most basic tasks, which he executed poorly.

Another issue in the build-up phase was the advanced positioning of Rabiot, who was drawn too far toward the final third, making him easy to shield. Unlike in the derby, he found himself receiving the ball with his back to the goal, almost always forcing him to pass backward.

Rabiot’s true value lies in his box-to-box quality: mobility is essential to maximizing his strengths, yet yesterday he was effectively caged by Amorim’s tactical design. Then there is Ramos, who touched the ball just three times (yes, three) in 30 minutes, despite the team holding 68% possession.

What is the point of maintaining possession if your best player remains on the periphery of the match and your centre-forward is never provided with a service? It was fortunate for Milan that, in the first half, Joseph displayed the worst of his repertoire, squandering two prime opportunities.

Realising the issues, Amorim tried to jolt the team into life by bringing on indispensable starters (Pulisic, Moreira and Gila) and dropping Rabiot deeper. It yielded no positive results, as the team’s build-up play remained predictable and their defense lacked cohesion.

Joseph made amends for his first-half finishing errors by scoring twice into an empty net. The first goal was gifted by a reckless back-pass from De Winter that Torriani failed to control; the second coming on a counter-attack, set up by an intelligent touch from Zachariassen.

Meanwhile, Milan’s first shot on target didn’t arrive until the 36th minute of the second half, courtesy of Hutchinson. By that point Ferencváros were down to ten men following Yusuf’s sending-off, and Amorim had deployed both Modrić and Camarda.

The coach opted for an improbable 4-2-4 formation with Moreira playing as a left-back. It was a move born of resignation, or rather, desperation. Which version of Milan will show up at Marassi on Sunday? It’s a question that naturally piques one’s curiosity.
